bounded_question: Can freely hanging vertical panels, staggered in depth, conceal the doorway without blocking discoverable passage?

execution.prompt: Keep this doorway crop, arch, warm edge catches, perspective and floor unchanged. Rework only the curtains and concealed light within the opening. Use two heavy working-black stage curtains hanging freely from above in long vertical pleats. The nearer left curtain hangs farther toward the center; the right curtain is farther back. Their loose vertical edges are staggered in depth, leaving a narrow irregular vertical opening that reaches the floor and suggests a person could pass between them into space out of sight. No fabric crosses or wraps horizontally across that route. Conceal most of the deeper room. Through one small interruption behind the left fold, reveal a thin, distant mineral-teal glimpse; behind the farther right fold, allow only a much softer, mostly obstructed smoky-plum trace. Colors are barely visible indirect atmosphere behind fabric, not bright beams, cones or colored curtain/jamb edges. Black fabric and dark spatial depth dominate. No tied-back presentation, horizontal bands, ribbons, swags, diagonal wrapping, flat closed curtain, new architecture, steps, bright sill, fixtures, people, mascot, text, logo or portal.

acceptance: Curtains hang vertically under gravity rather than forming bands across the doorway.
A continuous irregular passage reaches the floor; not a sealed curtain wall.
Teal is narrower and deeper; plum softer and more obstructed, with no paired mini-spotlights or colored jambs.
No invented subjects, fixtures, steps, lettering, bright sill or portal.
